Hi Sarah — thanks for sending these over and for flagging the timeline.

Quick responses:
- Output ownership: Redwood’s standard position is to grant customers a perpetual, worldwide, nonexclusive license to outputs, with customers retaining title to their uploaded customer content. We have flexibility on customer-attribution language but assignment of title for model-generated outputs is not our default.
- Training & feedback: we offer an opt-out from using customer inputs for model training at the enterprise level (usually documented on the Order Form). We can provide confirmation of retention windows and telemetry practices in an SOC2+ appendix.

Proposed next steps:
1) Connor (legal) and Karthik (product/ops) — can you review Sarah’s redlines and propose redline language that: a) preserves Redwood’s ability to operate and improve models while b) gives Skyline contractual assurances on training opt-out and telemetry?
2) Sarah — would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow (11/2) to walk legal through the specific clauses you care most about?
3) I’ll prepare a short one-pager summarizing our standard output license and training opt-out offering so procurement has a clear checkbox to accept on the Order Form.

Attachment: none (I’ll upload the one-pager to the Drive link below).

Sarah / Naomi — I reviewed the Skyline redlines and sketched a few compromises inline. High level:

- Output: We can accept language that gives Skyline a clear, perpetual, transferable right to use outputs for their business purposes (including productization), while carving out Redwood’s right to use de-identified telemetry for diagnostics and model improvement. Suggested text: "Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide license to outputs; Redwood retains a separate right to use aggregated/de-identified telemetry for model quality and security."

- Training opt-out: We can offer a contract-level opt-out (checked on Order Form) that prevents Redwood from incorporating customer-labeled inputs into training datasets for base model updates. We will still retain short-term ephemeral cache for serving (KV cache) per performance needs, with specified retention <= 30 days.

- Evidence/assurance: propose an appendix that outlines telemetry types collected, retention windows, and an audit protocol (quarterly report + ability to request redaction/wipe requests under defined SLA).

I attached a redlined Order Form with the opt-out checkbox and sample appendix. If Skyline needs assignment of title (rather than license) for outputs we should flag that as a commercial exception and run it through Exec (that’s a bigger ask).

Attachments: OrderForm_Skyline_20261101.pdf

Happy to jump on the call Naomi suggested. I’m available 11/3 9:30–11:30 PT.
